item.title: Pope warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
item.description:
Pontiff says artificial intelligence must remain at service of people in first official papal visit to country in 18 years Pope Leo has warned against losing humanity in a “paradise of machines” as he addressed global concerns over the dangers of artificial intelligence at the start of a three-day visit to France. “If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for people to be educated in ethical discernment, capable of seeing what is morally right,” he said in a speech at the Élysée. A pause. Then a dozen more Trumps. The pattern repeats several times. There are plugs for some of his priorities—such as cutting taxes and defending police officers—but one message stays on the screen for fully half of the 30-second commercial: AmericA will never be a communist country . item.title: Xi wraps up US visit with trip to National Archives
item.description:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping departed Washington this afternoon after a three-day trip that led to no significant breakthroughs on the two country’s disagreements, including on AI, Taiwan and Iran. Xi broached Taiwan to Trump, per a readout from Beijing, and Trump asked Xi to stop supporting Iran , US Ambassador to Beijing David Perdue said . Officials also discussed extending their trade truce until January and staying in touch about AI, Treasury Department Scott Bessent said earlier this week. But there were no major announcements with the countries still at odds on most fronts, including its growing nuclear arsenal. That could change later this year, when Xi said he would see Trump at the APEC summit in China and the G20 summit in the US. Xi also invited Trump back to China in the spring. Future meetings will likely cause similar heartburn for GOP lawmakers, many of whom said this week…

item.title: Lula says Trump wants to ‘colonise’ and capture Brazil’s resources by meddling in election
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington on Wednesday and was met personally on the tarmac by President Donald Trump. The agenda included an elaborate Rose Garden military review and official state dinner in the White House's East Room. Most of that chichi was just foreplay before Thursday's negotiations to extend the one-year trade war truce between the nations that's set to run out in November. It's quite the welcome for a leader of a country the administration calls America's chief adversary. Then again, it's no easy thing to follow the details of Trump's trade policy. His first term was different. Trump's Section 301 tariffs and most of the other tariffs starting in 2018 were aimed almost exclusively at China.
